---
title: "Evaluate fidelity and choose more simulations"
---

A useful surrogate must reproduce the aspects of a simulator required by your
scientific decision. Optimization loss alone does not establish this.

## Held-out performance

```python
report = surrogate.evaluate(split.test, n_samples=100, seed=42)
print(report.by_output)
print(report.worst_groups(5))
report.save("evaluation.json")
fig = report.plot()  # requires [plots]
fig.savefig("evaluation.png")
```

Reports include the resolved architecture, a fingerprint of the fitted model,
training settings, fitting/evaluation dataset fingerprints and sample settings.
Overlap with training or validation groups generates a warning.
Validation is used to choose weights and tune settings, so it is not an
independent test. Simulation replicates remain together across partitions.

MAE and RMSE are measured in original units using full autonomous predictions.
Large-unit outputs dominate aggregate errors; inspect each output and define
acceptable errors for your task. Replicate-mean errors are reported for groups
with identical conditioning inputs. Finite replicate means themselves have
simulation noise.

Stochastic models additionally report empirical CRPS, 90% pointwise predictive
coverage and interval width. The intervals describe variability under the
fitted generator, not confidence about surrogate accuracy or simultaneous
coverage of a whole trajectory. Check temporal dependence, rare events and
cross-output structure in application-specific analyses as well.

Do not compare MSE, velocity-fitting error and negative log density as though
they were the same score. The benchmark script compares common held-out metrics
and records the budget used by each family. Short benchmarks test the pipeline,
not a universal ranking of architectures.

## Explicit scientific constraints

```python
report = surrogate.evaluate(split.test, constraints={
    "nonnegative": ["S_t", "I_t", "R_t", "D_t"],
    "nondecreasing": ["D_t"],
    "conserved_total": {
        "outputs": ["S_t", "I_t", "R_t", "D_t"],
        "value": 1000, "atol": 0.001,
    },
})
print(report.metadata["constraints"])
```

These are SIRDS-specific examples, not assumptions made for every dataset.
Checks report violation fractions; they do not clip or correct predictions.
Nonnegative/nondecreasing checks use strict zero thresholds. The conservation
tolerance is explicitly supplied by the researcher.

## Where to simulate next

```python
from metis import assess_coverage, suggest_simulations
coverage = assess_coverage(split.train, candidate_inputs)
suggestions = suggest_simulations(split.train, candidate_inputs, n=10)
```

You supply scientifically valid candidates. Distances are Euclidean after
scaling each input by its training range; constant dimensions use scale one.
The greedy rule selects the candidate furthest from existing inputs, adds it
to the reference set, and repeats. It seeks coverage gaps, not maximal posterior
uncertainty. It does not estimate model error, simulation cost or an optimal
replicate allocation. Outside-range flags are marginal checks, not proof that
a point inside the box is well supported jointly.

Also inspect `worst_groups()` for measured error patterns. More coverage, more
replicates, a different architecture and better optimization solve different
problems. Once you adapt using test errors, obtain a fresh independent test bank
before claiming final performance.

## Conditioned models

For observed-sequence models, evaluation banks include both observed and
predicted channels in the original fitted order. METIS supplies observed channels
to each prediction and computes metrics for predicted channels only. Report
which path was supplied, and whether it would be known in deployment. In
particular, flow matching can use the complete path; that evaluation is not a
causal forecasting test. See [conditioning](conditioning.qmd).

Reports record both the evaluation batch size and the model's internal inference
batch size/device. Changing either batch size can change seeded Monte Carlo
draws; retain these settings when reproducing sampled diagnostics. Legacy imports
record their inference batch setting separately from unknown historical training
settings.
